claim: All capacity unit and request unit quotas are measured per second, so a quota of 40,000 read capacity units means 40,000 reads per second.

claim: You can request any number of read capacity units or write capacity units for your tables through a service quota increase. The default table values are initial quotas, not maximum limits.
question: Are the default DynamoDB throughput quotas a hard maximum?

claim: You start each UTC day with 4 available capacity decreases per table, 1 more becomes available each hour (up to 4 available at any time), and over a full 24-hour day you can decrease up to 27 times.
question: How many times per day can you decrease the provisioned capacity of a DynamoDB table?

qualifiers.scope: per table, and separately per global secondary index, per UTC day

evidence.quote: You start each day with 4 available decreases. Each hour, 1 additional decrease becomes available, up to the maximum of 4 available at any time. Over a full 24-hour day, this allows you to decrease up to 27 times (4 in the first hour, plus 1 for each of the remaining 23 hours).

claim: For single-Region tables that are not global tables, you can design for up to two simultaneous processes reading the same DynamoDB Streams shard. For global tables, limit simultaneous readers to one.
question: How many processes can read one DynamoDB Streams shard at the same time?

qualifiers.condition: two for single-Region tables that are not global tables; one recommended for global tables; exceeding can cause throttling

evidence.quote: For single-Region tables that are not global tables, you can design for up to two simultaneous processes to read from the same DynamoDB Streams shard at the same time. Exceeding this limit can result in request throttling. For global tables, we recommend you limit the number of simultaneous readers to one to avoid request throttling.

claim: A full export to Amazon S3 supports up to 300 concurrent export tasks, or a total of 100 TB from all in-flight table exports. Both limits are checked before an export is queued.

evidence.quote: Full export: up to 300 concurrent export tasks, or up to a total of 100TB from all in-flight table exports, can be exported. Both of these limits are checked before an export is queued.

claim: For incremental export to Amazon S3, the export period window is 15 minutes minimum and 24 hours maximum. It supports up to 300 concurrent export jobs or 100TB from all in-flight table exports.
question: What is the export period window of an incremental export to Amazon S3?

qualifiers.condition: window is 15 minutes minimum and 24 hours maximum

evidence.quote: Incremental export: DynamoDB Incremental Export to Amazon S3 can support up to 300 concurrent export jobs or up to a total of 100TB from all in-flight table exports. The export period window limits are 15 minutes minimum and 24 hours maximum.

claim: DynamoDB supports up to 50 concurrent restores totaling 50 TB through on-demand or continuous backups. AWS Backup supports up to 50 concurrent restores totaling 25 TB.
question: How many concurrent restores and how much total restore size does DynamoDB allow?

qualifiers.scope: concurrent restores, DynamoDB backups versus AWS Backup
qualifiers.condition: 50 TB total through DynamoDB backups; 25 TB total through AWS Backup

evidence.quote: DynamoDB supports up to 50 concurrent restores totaling 50 TB through DynamoDB on-demand or continuous backups. AWS Backup supports up to 50 concurrent restores totaling 25 TB.
